name: LArIAT
summary: LArIAT used a liquid-argon TPC in a charged-particle test beam at Fermilab to calibrate the detector response and measure particle-argon interactions important for neutrino experiments. It reused the ArgoNeuT cryostat and detector with dedicated modifications.
physics_targets: Calibration and reconstruction for liquid-argon neutrino detectors
Hadron-argon cross sections and final-state interactions
detection_principle: A tagged tertiary beam supplies pions, muons, electrons, protons and kaons. Ionization tracks and scintillation light in liquid argon are compared with independently measured incoming-particle properties, allowing calorimetric calibration, particle identification and hadron-interaction measurements.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: Fermilab marks the T-1034 beam experiment completed on 23 June 2017. Later papers analyze its stored test-beam data.

collaboration.name: LArIAT Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: Measured the negative-pion total hadronic cross section on argon with the thin-slice method, providing a direct input to detector-interaction modelling.
Measured MeV-scale deposits from stopped negative-pion and muon capture, demonstrating a particle-discrimination observable for neutrino LArTPCs.

science_scope: This is a neutrino-detector technology and calibration experiment. Its charged-particle beam measurements are not neutrino cross-section measurements or evidence of neutrino oscillation.
